name: FINOS Multi-Agent Reference Architecture (CALM Model)
description: Machine-readable CALM v1.2 representation of the FINOS Multi-Agent Reference Architecture and its April 2026 Threat Model (36 controls C1-C36 mapped across all 58 threats T-UIL-01..T-XL-04 and AIGF mitigations MI-18..MI-21).

nodes.name: User
nodes.description: Individual analyst, employee, customer, or automated calling process initiating a request and reviewing outputs.

nodes.name: Application
nodes.description: Presentation and orchestration surface capturing user intent, enforcing HITL checkpoints, and sanitising rendered outputs.

nodes.name: Agent Registry
nodes.description: Catalog of approved agents, signed FSI Agent Cards, capabilities, autonomy ceilings (A0-A4), and SR 11-7 model inventory links.

nodes.name: Agent Gateway
nodes.description: Zero-trust entry point into the Agent Layer enforcing mTLS/SPIFFE workload identity, signed Agent Card verification, and routing.

nodes.name: Agent Gateway Guardrails and Policies
nodes.description: Policy-as-Code and AI security inspection engine validating prompts, mandate scope/freshness (MI-18), and rate limits prior to agent dispatch.

nodes.name: Supervisor and Routing Agent
nodes.description: Orchestrates Supervisor/Worker, Skills-Based Routing, and Agent-as-a-Tool patterns with strict-subset authority attenuation (MI-18).

nodes.name: Specialized Worker Agents
nodes.description: Scoped subordinate agents executing domain-bounded sub-tasks under attenuated workload identities and strict data domain boundaries.

nodes.name: Unified Agent Runtime
nodes.description: Sandboxed execution environment managing task state, pause/resume integrity, collaboration handoffs, and resource quotas.

nodes.name: Secure Execution and Built-in Tools Layer
nodes.description: Intercepts and validates all tool call requests (Shell, I/O, Web Search), enforcing JIT task-scoped permissions, atomic shared-limit reservations (MI-18), and tool authorization levels (MI-19).

nodes.name: Workspace File System
nodes.description: Sandboxed path-scoped file storage with DLP scanning and full agent identity attribution.

nodes.name: Adaptive Learning
nodes.description: Generates versioned, human-reviewed configuration refinement signals from validated execution outcomes.

nodes.name: MCP Client Bridge
nodes.description: Secure bridge from Unified Agent Runtime to the external MCP Gateway enforcing data minimisation and parameter schema checks.

nodes.name: Short-Term Memory (In-Session Context)
nodes.description: Manages immediate reasoning context with untrusted input sanitisation and context-poisoning guards.

nodes.name: Long-Term Memory Store
nodes.description: Maintains cryptographically bound, cross-session isolated session summaries and personalization records.

nodes.name: Authoritative Source Bases
nodes.description: Structured, unstructured, and graph-based enterprise knowledge repositories with cryptographic ingestion integrity.

nodes.name: Vector Databases
nodes.description: Semantic retrieval store enforcing ABAC, embedding encryption, RAG validation, and source-trust weighting.

nodes.name: Model Registry
nodes.description: Catalog of vetted, cryptographically signed models with SBOMs and load-time signature verification.

nodes.name: LLM Gateway
nodes.description: Controlled routing interface for approved model inference endpoints with mTLS and quota enforcement.

nodes.name: LLM Guardrails and Policies
nodes.description: Pre- and post-inference prompt injection filter, system-prompt leakage redaction, and policy-as-code enforcement.

nodes.name: MCP Server Registry
nodes.description: Catalog of signed, approved MCP servers with globally unique namespaced tool IDs and capability declarations.

nodes.name: MCP Gateway
nodes.description: Mandatory choke point for all MCP server connections enforcing mTLS/SPIFFE SVIDs and zero-trust micro-segmentation.

nodes.name: MCP Guardrails and Policies
nodes.description: Validates MCP tool parameter schemas, domain authorization, and minimum(user,agent) effective authorization (MI-19).

nodes.name: Feedback Engine
nodes.description: Aggregates authenticated, multi-source evaluation signals with statistical anomaly detection.

nodes.name: Human Supervision Gate
nodes.description: Non-bypassable platform enforcement for HITL/HOTL checkpoints and regulatory reporting sign-off, cryptographically binding approvals to actions.

nodes.name: Runtime Protection and Circuit Breaker Engine
nodes.description: Stateful sliding-window monitor and fail-closed circuit breaker (MI-20 ST-01..ST-05) halting individual or collective multi-agent systemic exposure breaches.

nodes.name: Observability Layer (WORM Logs, Signed Traces, Metrics, SIEM & Correlation Engine)
nodes.description: Append-only WORM audit store, cryptographically signed trace/log collector, IETF SCITT (RFC 9162) decision receipt log (MI-21), longitudinal anomaly detector, and SOAR correlation engine.

relationships.description: User initiates requests and reviews HITL approval prompts at the Application surface.
Application forwards authenticated requests to the Agent Gateway.
Agent Gateway resolves signed FSI Agent Cards and autonomy ceilings from the Agent Registry.
Agent Gateway evaluates every inbound request against Agent Gateway Guardrails and Policies before routing.
Validated requests are dispatched into the Unified Agent Runtime Supervisor Agent.
Supervisor delegates sub-tasks to Worker Agents with strict-subset authority and MNPI data-domain verification.
Supervisor and Worker Agents execute inside the sandboxed Unified Agent Runtime.
All agent tool calls and state mutations are intercepted by Secure Execution for commitment-time mandate verification (MI-18) and tool scope validation (MI-19).
Secure Execution mediates path-scoped reads and DLP-scanned writes to the Workspace File System.
Unified Agent Runtime reads and writes sanitised Short-Term and cryptographically isolated Long-Term Memory.
Agent Layer retrieves grounded context from Authoritative Source Bases and Vector DBs with ABAC, DLP scanning, and RAG sanitisation.
Vector DB indexes validated and hashed documents from Authoritative Source Bases.
Agent Layer submits model inference requests exclusively through the LLM Gateway.
LLM Gateway verifies model signatures against Model Registry and enforces LLM Guardrails on prompts and outputs.
LLM Gateway and Guardrails verify signed model metadata and SBOM status in the Model Registry.
MCP Client Bridge routes all external tool calls exclusively through the MCP Gateway choke point.
MCP Gateway validates tool parameters, domain scope, and effective authorization via MCP Guardrails.
MCP Guardrails resolve signed, namespaced tool definitions in the MCP Server Registry.
Evaluation Layer (Runtime Protection Circuit Breakers, Human Supervision Gate, and Feedback Engine) monitors and intervenes on the Unified Agent Runtime.
Human Supervision Gate enforces non-bypassable approval checkpoints on high-risk actions and regulatory outputs.
Feedback Engine provides multi-source weighted evaluation signals to Adaptive Learning.
All architectural layers emit cryptographically signed logs, trace spans, metrics, events, and IETF SCITT (RFC 9162) decision receipts (MI-21) to the Observability Layer.

C1.description: Implement input validation libraries and custom rules at the application layer

C2.description: Use a specialised AI security tool, integrated as part of a gateway (Agent, MCP, or LLM) or as a standalone firewall, to inspect, validate, and sanitise prompts and responses for content-based threats

C3.description: Design workflows to require human approval for high-risk actions

C4.description: Integrate with an enterprise Identity Provider (IDP) enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

C5.description: Feed user activity and agent logs into a security analytics platform (SIEM) for behavioural analytics and anomaly detection

C6.description: Configure rate limiting and throttling on API endpoints

C7.description: Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF) with rulesets to block common attack vectors

C8.description: Use a Policy-as-Code engine to enforce Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policies for write access

C9.description: Log all critical changes to a centralised, write-once, read-many (WORM) system

C10.description: Implement automated configuration scanning to detect unauthorised changes

C11.description: Use platform-native network policies (Kubernetes network policies, security groups) to enforce micro-segmentation

C12.description: Enforce mutual TLS (mTLS) for all connections using strong, verifiable workload identities (SPIFFE SVIDs)

C13.description: Manage and version-control all security policies (authorisation, content, behaviour) as code in a version control system

C14.description: Use sandboxing or containerisation technologies to isolate agent processes and tool execution

C15.description: Implement runtime monitoring to detect and alert on anomalous agent behaviour or goal deviation

C16.description: Ensure child agents are created with a scoped, delegated workload identity and a subset of the parent agent's permissions

C17.description: Grant just-in-time, task-scoped permissions for tool execution

C18.description: Implement automated data validation and sanitisation pipelines for knowledge sources

C19.description: Integrate with Data Loss Prevention (DLP) solutions to scan agent outputs for sensitive data

C20.description: Ensure logs contain full cryptographic workload identity and rich contextual details for forensic investigation

C21.description: Implement automated response playbooks (SOAR) for high-confidence alerts

C22.description: Implement resource quotas and limits (CPU, memory, execution time) within the agent runtime environment

C23.description: Sanitise all agent-generated output to remove or neutralise malicious code before it is displayed to users or passed to other systems

C24.description: Encrypt sensitive data, including models, both at rest and in transit

C25.description: Implement a strict vetting and scanning process for all new models and components before they are registered in the platform

C26.description: Enforce strict, non-bypassable workflows for tasks that require human supervision

C27.description: Implement a multi-source feedback engine that aggregates and weights signals from diverse sources to generate a trusted score for agent interactions

C28.description: Implement network egress filtering to restrict agent outbound connections to an approved destination allowlist

C29.description: Use a dedicated secrets management platform for all credentials, API keys, and certificates; never inject secrets as environment variables accessible to the agent process

C30.description: Enforce cryptographic signing and integrity verification for all registered models; validate signatures at load time and reject any model whose signature cannot be verified

C31.description: Maintain a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for all agent components, dependencies, and models; integrate SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning into the CI/CD pipeline

C32.description: Enforce data minimisation at the agent runtime layer; pass only the data fields required for each tool call and strip all fields not needed for the immediate task before dispatch

C33.description: Apply RAG-specific validation; validate and sanitise retrieved documents before injection into the agent context window and monitor retrieval patterns for anomalous query distributions

C34.description: Enforce strict cross-session isolation in long-term memory; cryptographically bind all memory entries to the originating user and session identity

C35.description: Enforce strict parameter schema validation for all MCP tool calls; reject any call where parameters contain data from domains not authorised for that tool

C36.description: Require signed Agent Card verification for all agent-to-agent calls; reject connections from agents presenting unverifiable, expired, or revoked identities; use a short-lived credential rotation policy
